_readme: THE EVENT BOOK, phase 1 (30 events). Schema: lib/star/life/types.ts LifeEvent. Conditions: lib/star/life/cond.ts. Checked by tests/star/lifeEvents.mts (validate.ts). 15 come from docs/plans/living-world-sample-events-2026-11-20.json (minigames that need new art became skill checks), 15 are new in the same schema. Money is weeks of your own wage. Every brand and paper is invented.

events.title: "Can I borrow the motor?"
setup: Your phone lights up on the dash: {mate.name}.
{mate.short}: "Mate. Big favour. It's my mum's sixtieth Saturday night. Can I turn up in yours? I'll have it back Sunday, washed."

outcomes.text: It comes back Sunday, washed, with a full tank and a can of KIB on the seat.
Sunday night. A photo arrives first. The front wing is against a bollard. "I am so, so sorry."
"Yeah. No. Fair enough." He hangs up a bit quick.

choices.label: "I'll do better. I'll drive you there myself."

outcomes.text: You drop him at the door. His mum makes you stay for cake. There is a photo of you two on her fridge now.

callbacks.line: "Was going to ask you for a lift. Then I remembered the car."
In a tight chance he shoots instead of squaring it while his grudge is 20 or more.
"Mum still asks after you."

events.title: He wants to make it right
setup: {mate.short} is waiting by your table with an envelope.
"That's the repair. All of it. And I've told the gaffer it was me, before the papers make it you."

outcomes.text: Square. He looks relieved, and a bit small.
He does not know what to say. He will not forget it.

callbacks.line: He is the first to stand up for you in the dressing room.
"Still owe you for the car. Don't think I've forgotten."

events.title: "Don't say anything. Just listen."
events.speaker: agent
setup: {agent.name}: "Don't say anything. Just listen. A bigger club had a man at your last three. They'll come in the summer. I can let that be known, or I can keep it very quiet. Your call."

outcomes.text: By Thursday it is on every feed. The gaffer does not look at you in training.

choices.label: "Keep it quiet. I've a season to finish."

outcomes.text: "Your funeral." He means it kindly. Mostly.

choices.label: Hang up. Go and tell the gaffer yourself.

outcomes.text: He listens, nods once. "Nobody has ever told me first."
He takes your silence as a yes. It is in the papers by Friday.
He takes your silence as a no, and sounds hurt about it.

callbacks.line: "You like the papers. Read about the team in them on Saturday."
"You came to me first, once. I've not forgotten."
"Going to run this one past the gaffer too?"
His opening ask for you is 5% lower: "I work as hard as I'm trusted."

events.title: The man from the tabloid
events.speaker: hack
setup: {hack.name} of the {hack.outlet} steps across you in the mixed zone, phone up, recording.
"{you.short}. Not a shot on target. Are you worth the money?"

choices.label: "Not today I wasn't. That's on me."

outcomes.text: He lowers the phone a little. The piece runs under 'NO EXCUSES'. Fair.
"Nothing to say, then." He says it loudly, for the others.

choices.label: "Have you ever kicked a ball in your life?"

outcomes.text: The clip has two million views by breakfast. Your own fans love it. He does not.
He sighs. Nobody prints that. Your gaffer likes it, though.
It goes out as a promise. The fans screenshot it. Saturday had better go well.

callbacks.line: "Fair play for last time. Not many front up."
His match reports mark you half a point kinder for 10 weeks.
"Remember me? I remember you."

events.title: "Sources close to the dressing room"
setup: Your phone will not stop. {hack.outlet}: "{you.short} 'THINKS HE'S BIGGER THAN THE CLUB', say team-mates."
{if source}The quotes sound a lot like {source.short}.{/if}

outcomes.text: It burns for a week and goes out.

choices.label: Ring him. Offer the sit-down interview he wanted.

outcomes.text: An hour in a hotel bar. The follow-up piece is called 'The other side of {you.short}'.
You put the paper on {source.short}'s seat in the canteen. He does not deny it. The room goes quiet.

callbacks.line: He will not sit at your table since the canteen.
"Still got the tape of that sit-down. Best thing I wrote all year."

events.title: The lad on his own
setup: {kid.name}, {kid.age}, up from the academy, is eating on his own with his headphones in.
{mate.short} waves you over to the usual table.

outcomes.text: He takes one headphone out. Ten minutes later he is telling you about his nan's jollof. He watches where you sit every day after that.

choices.label: Shout him over to the lads' table.

outcomes.text: He comes. The lads rip his trainers apart for ten minutes. He is grinning by the end.
He pretends not to hear, goes red, and leaves his food.
Nobody notices. That is rather the point.

callbacks.line: "Day one, you sat with me. I don't forget that."
He runs the length of the pitch to you when he scores.
"The lads still go on about my trainers. Worth it."

events.title: A day at the races
setup: You and {mate.short} in the owners' bar. He has a tip from his cousin: number 7, 'Offside Trap', 12 to 1 in the fourth.
{if owns:horse}Your own {you.horse} runs in the fifth.{/if}

choices.label: Put a proper bet on his tip.

outcomes.text: It wins by a nose. He is on the table. You are both on the back pages, grinning.
Fifth of nine. The money is gone. He cannot look at you. "My cousin is dead to me."

choices.label: A fiver each way, for a laugh.

outcomes.text: A good day. Nothing happens, in the best way. He tells you he is thinking of leaving in the summer; you are the first to know.

choices.label: "Forget his cousin. Back mine in the fifth."

outcomes.text: {you.horse} by two lengths. {mate.short} had fifty on it.
Last. "Lovely looking animal, though," he says, tearing up his slip.

callbacks.line: "How's the donkey?"
"My cousin says sorry about the horse. He's not allowed tips any more."
"Offside Trap. Still got the slip in my wallet."
If he is sold: a goodbye text that names the day.

events.title: He wants your number
events.speaker: rival
setup: {rival.name}, the new signing, is stood at your peg holding the number {you.number} shirt.
"I've worn this since I was nine. The club said to ask you. So I'm asking." {kitman.short} is pretending to fold socks.

outcomes.text: He hangs it back up, slowly. "Okay. We'll see who's wearing it in May."

choices.label: Hand it over. "Numbers don't score goals."

outcomes.text: He did not expect that. The kit man raises an eyebrow. The fans who bought your shirt are not happy.
Bar, first go. He shakes your hand properly.
He hits it. You don't. A deal is a deal. The fans who bought your shirt are not happy.
You say nothing. He hangs the shirt back on your peg, slowly. "Right." {kitman.short} folds the same sock twice.

callbacks.line: "May. Like I said."
He taps the number on his back when he walks past.
He points at his own number, at you, on the bench.

events.title: Who wears it in May
events.speaker: rival
setup: Last day of the season. {rival.short} is at your peg again, the goals chart from the canteen wall in his hand.
{if outscored(rival)}You scored more. He knows it.{/if}{if !outscored(rival)}He scored more. Everybody knows it.{/if}

outcomes.text: "Keep the shirt. You earned it." He means it. Something between you settles.
He shakes it, then asks for the shirt again. In front of everyone.

choices.label: Pin the chart back on the wall. Upside down.

outcomes.text: The lads howl. He does not.

choices.label: Give him the shirt. "You won it."

outcomes.text: The kit man sews your new number on that night. The gaffer nods at you in the corridor.
You walk past him to the showers. Behind you, the chart goes in the bin.

callbacks.line: He still has the chart. He keeps it in his locker.
"Most lads would have found a way out of that bet. You didn't."

events.title: Dad's old club
setup: Dad rings. He never rings. "The Sunday side. The one I took you to when you were five. The council want the pitch money or they fold. I'm not asking. I'm just telling you."

choices.label: Pay it. Today. Say nothing publicly.

outcomes.text: He goes quiet for a long time. "Your mum'll cry when I tell her." They paint your name on the hut.

choices.label: Pay it, and bring the cameras.

outcomes.text: Lovely pictures. Dad stands at the back of every one.
"No. No, course." The club folds in the spring. He tells you in passing.

callbacks.line: "The kids at the Sunday side still talk about you."
The Sunday side's kids form your guard of honour.
"I'd ask, but I know how you are with money."

events.title: The wrong boots
setup: {mate.short} chucks you a prototype pair from his brand, Vanta. "Try them. One session. Nobody's watching." They feel unbelievable.
Somebody was watching. A photo is on a fan account by tea time. {agent.short} texts: "Your boot people have seen it. Tell me that's edited."

outcomes.text: "It had better not." A fine comes off your next payment.

choices.label: "They're better than yours. Match them or I walk."

outcomes.text: A day of silence. Then a new offer, fee up.
"Then walk." They pull the bonus they owed you. Vanta do not ring.
They believe you. His brand does not see the funny side, and neither does he when he finds out why.

callbacks.line: "Ask one of your sponsors."
"Last time you bluffed, it cost us both."

events.title: 2:14 a.m.
events.speaker: stranger
setup: A text from a number you do not know. A photo: you, at the roulette table, clock on the wall behind you. 2:14 a.m. Match on Saturday.
"Nice night? The {hack.outlet} would pay me well for this. You can pay me better."

outcomes.text: The photo never appears.
He takes the money and sells it anyway. Now there are two stories.

choices.label: Go to the gaffer before it breaks.

outcomes.text: He is furious for four minutes and useful for ten. The club puts out a line before the paper does.

choices.label: "Sell it. I was there. So what."

outcomes.text: Front page Friday. Two goals Saturday. Sunday's headline: 'WHAT A GAMBLE'.
Front page Friday. A stinker Saturday. They boo you off.
Nothing. Then nothing. Then Saturday's paper.
He never texts again. You check your phone forty times a day for a month.

callbacks.line: "Casino this week, is it? Don't."
The next one asks double: "I hear you pay."
"Going to the casino before every game now, are we?"

events.title: It's probably nothing
events.speaker: physio
setup: Your hamstring tightens in the warm-up. {physio.name} presses a thumb into it and watches your face.
"Play Saturday and it's probably fine. Probably. Sit out and it's definitely fine. {boss.short} will ask me. What do I tell him?"

choices.label: "Tell him the truth. I'll sit this one out."

outcomes.text: You watch from the stand. Monday it feels brand new.
It holds. Just.
Sixty-third minute. You know before you hit the ground. Weeks of rehab.

choices.label: "Bench. Twenty minutes if we need it."

outcomes.text: She nods. "That I can sell."
You shrug and jog off. {physio.short} tells {boss.short} the truth anyway, and that you would not.

callbacks.line: "You do the rehab. Most don't."
"Not again. I'm telling him. You don't get to choose this time."
"Fit, are you? Properly fit? I'll be asking her, not you."

events.title: Chain 1 of 3: "Size nine?"
setup: Forty minutes to kick-off. {kid.name}'s sole has come clean off. He has one pair. He is trying to tape it and his hands are shaking.
He sees you looking. "You're a nine, aren't you?"

outcomes.text: He plays the game of his life in them. You play in your old pair, and your feet know it.

choices.label: "Tape's in the physio bag. Sort yourself out."

outcomes.text: He plays in a taped boot and comes off at half time with a blister the size of a coin.

callbacks.line: "Got my own boots now, if you were wondering."

events.title: Chain 2 of 3: He tries to give them back
setup: {kid.short} is waiting with your boots, cleaned better than you have ever cleaned them. "I get paid Friday. I'll get my own."

outcomes.text: He holds them like they might break.

choices.label: Sign them first. "For when you're famous."

outcomes.text: "When, not if?" "When." The lads saw. You are 'Mr Autograph' for a week.
Fair is fair. He looks at his own taped pair.

callbacks.line: "Still wearing them. Lucky ones."

events.title: Chain 3 of 3: Years later
setup: The tunnel. {kid.name} is a man now, and a captain. He is stood next to you in the line.
{if mem(kid,'you-signed-the-boots-when-not-if')}He lifts one foot. Your old boots. Your signature, nearly worn off. "When, not if. You said."{/if}
{if mem(kid,'you-gave-him-the-boots')}"I've still got them. They're in a glass case at my mum's."{/if}
{if mem(kid,'you-told-him-to-tape-it')}He does not look at you. "Tape's in the physio bag," he says, to nobody.{/if}

outcomes.text: After the match he tells the cameras the story. It is the most shared clip of the season.
He hugs you before the handshake line. The cameras catch it.
He marks you all game like it is personal. It is. He scores and runs past you to the away end.

callbacks.line: "Tape's in the physio bag, isn't it?"
"My mum's had three journalists round about those boots."

events.title: The long way round
setup: {mate.short} gets in. {if carTier>=3}He runs a hand along the dash. "This is a different life, mate."{/if}{if carTier<=2}He has to move a pile of kit off the seat to sit down.{/if}
You take the long way, past the ground and out along the coast road.

outcomes.text: Forty minutes of his awful playlist. He sings every word. It is the best you have felt all week.

choices.label: Ask how he is really doing.

outcomes.text: Quiet for a mile. Then it all comes out: his dad, the move, the nights. You just drive.
"Fine, mate. All good." He changes the subject to the weekend.

choices.label: Have a moan about the gaffer.

outcomes.text: You both do the gaffer's voice. He is better at it. You laugh until the lights change.
He tells a mate, who tells the assistant. It reaches the gaffer by Monday.

callbacks.line: "Cheers for the other day. In the car. I needed that."
"Enjoy your drive, did you? Walls have ears."
"Put my playlist on next time. You know you want to."

events.title: Blue lights
setup: {mate.short} dares you to open it up on the bypass. You do. Blue lights in the mirror a mile later.
The officer leans in, then does a double take. "Well, well."

outcomes.text: A fine and three points. The officer shakes your hand anyway.
He does. He wants a selfie for his son. You are let off with a warning.
He does. So does the paper by Tuesday: 'DO YOU KNOW WHO I AM?'

choices.label: Ask him to say he was driving.

outcomes.text: He takes the points for you. He does not say a word all the way home.
"Mate. No." The officer heard all of it. Double the fine.

callbacks.line: "Six points, mate. Six. You owe me."
"Still can't believe that copper wanted a selfie."

events.title: The whip-round
setup: The squad group chat: "Whip-round for {mate.short}'s birthday. Drop it in the kit room by Friday. No excuses."
Eleven people have already sent a thumbs up.

outcomes.text: He opens the card in the canteen and reads every name out.
Somebody screenshots it. You are 'Card at Home' for a month.

choices.label: Sort him a proper night out.

outcomes.text: A table, his family, a cake shaped like a boot. He makes a speech and cries.

callbacks.line: "Got your card today, have you?"
"Best birthday I've had since I was a kid. Cheers for that."

events.title: Boots in the ice bath
setup: {joker.short} has frozen {victim.short}'s new boots into a block in the ice bath. The whole room is waiting for him to walk in.
{joker.short} hands you his phone. "You film it."

outcomes.text: {victim.short} walks in, sees it, and laughs a second too late.

choices.label: Get the boots out before he arrives.

outcomes.text: {joker.short} calls you a killjoy. {victim.short} never knows how close it was, until somebody tells him.
Three million views. The gaffer has a word about 'the dressing room staying in the dressing room'.

callbacks.line: "Still got that video up, have you?"
"Heard about the boots. You didn't have to do that. Thanks."

events.title: A call at midnight
events.speaker: mate
setup: {mate.name}, at ten to midnight. He is outside somewhere; you can hear traffic.
"I'm in a hole, mate. Betting. I owe the wrong people about two weeks of what you earn. I wouldn't ask if there was anyone else."

outcomes.text: The money is in his account before he has finished saying thank you.

choices.label: "Ring the club welfare officer. Tonight. I'll come with you."

outcomes.text: He goes. It takes a long time, but he goes.
"I asked for money, not a lecture." He hangs up.
Silence. Then the line goes.
You say nothing for too long. "Forget it. Forget I rang." The line goes dead.

callbacks.line: "I've not had a bet in ten weeks. Thought you should know."
He answers, but he does not look up from his phone.

events.title: The loan
setup: {mate.short} sits down opposite you with two coffees. "About the money."

outcomes.text: He slides an envelope over. Every penny, and a bit more. "Interest."
"Not yet. Soon. I swear." You both know it is not soon.

choices.label: "Forget it. Just stay out of the bookies."

outcomes.text: He looks at the table for a long time. The money is gone; he is not.

callbacks.line: He is the first to stand up for you. "He's helped more people in here than you know."
"I know, I know. I'm sorting it."

events.title: The towel over his head
events.speaker: mate
setup: We won. {mate.short} played ten minutes. He plays where you play.
He is sat in the corner with a towel over his head while everyone else sings.

choices.label: Sit with him for a bit.

outcomes.text: Neither of you says much. You miss the singing. When you get up he says "cheers" to the floor.
The towel comes off. The look stays with you.
Probably what he wanted. Probably.
He does not look up. But he nods.

callbacks.line: "Train harder, you said. I did."
"Cheers for the other night. In the corner."

events.title: Thirty years at the club
setup: {kitman.name} has been at the club thirty years. He asks, a bit embarrassed, for a signed shirt for his grandson's hospital ward.

choices.label: Sign ten. Take them in yourself.

outcomes.text: The nurses line the corridor. His grandson will not let go of your hand.
"Lovely. Ta." He folds it like it is made of glass.
"Course." The lads heard. The dressing room goes a bit cold on you.

callbacks.line: "The ward's still got your shirts on the wall."
Your boots are not on your peg. He finds them, slowly.

events.title: Mum's birthday
setup: Dad, quietly: "It's your mum's birthday Sunday. You're away Saturday. Just so you know."

outcomes.text: She rings you from the hotel balcony in a dressing gown. Dad is in the background, pretending not to be pleased.

choices.label: Flowers, and a video call from the team bus.

outcomes.text: Half the squad shout happy birthday into your phone. She loves it.
Dad texts at nine on Sunday night: "She waited up."

callbacks.line: "Don't worry, love. I know you're busy."
"I'm still showing everyone the photos from that weekend."

events.title: Ten per cent
events.speaker: agent
setup: Your accountant, by text: "Your boot deal paid ten per cent more than {agent.short} told you. He kept the difference. Three seasons of it."

outcomes.text: He goes white, then pays it back by Friday. "A misunderstanding."
He denies it, then shouts, then hangs up. Your next deal will be harder to get.
You check every line of the next contract yourself. He notices.

choices.label: Sack him, and tell the papers why.

outcomes.text: It is a big story for two days. People who run football like a player who reads his contracts.

choices.label: Ask him nicely if there is a mistake.

outcomes.text: He apologises for 'an admin error' and pays half of it back.
"No mistake, kid. That's the fee." He sounds amused.

callbacks.line: "I've been straight with you since. Every penny."
He now works for the other side of the table.

events.title: The car park
events.speaker: stranger
setup: After the game, in the car park. A man in a quilted jacket walks with you to your car like he knows you.
"Yellow card before the twentieth minute on Saturday. Five weeks of your wages, cash. Nobody gets hurt."

outcomes.text: You get booked in the twelfth minute. Nobody says a word. The money is in a shoebox under your bed.
The betting people have been watching him for months. Your name is in their file. The club suspends you while it is looked at.

choices.label: Walk away. Report it to the club.

outcomes.text: The integrity people take a statement. The gaffer shakes your hand in front of the staff.
He watches you drive off. You check the mirror for a long time.

callbacks.line: "You've done it once. That makes the second time easy."
"I'll be watching your first twenty minutes. Every week."
The papers call you 'the one who said no'.

events.title: He knows where you park
events.speaker: stranger
setup: A withheld number, late.
{if mem(you,'took-the-yellow-card-money')}"Same again. A penalty given away this time. You know what happens if you say no now."{/if}
{if mem(you,'reported-the-fixer')}"You talked. I know where you park. I know where your mum parks."{/if}
{if mem(you,'said-nothing-to-the-fixer')}"Last chance. Ten weeks of your money for one bad pass."{/if}

choices.label: Go to the police. All of it.

outcomes.text: Statements, a panic alarm at your mum's, a court date in the spring. You are in the papers the right way round.
Ten weeks of money in a sports bag. You do not sleep.
It is the game the investigators were watching. It is over by Monday: suspended, every paper, every feed.
Nothing. Weeks of nothing. You still check the mirror.
Your car is burnt out on the drive at four in the morning. The insurance will not touch it.
You say nothing. He breathes down the line for a long time, then laughs and hangs up. You do not sleep.

callbacks.line: He is in court in the spring. Your name is in the paper, the right way round.
"Heard about your car. Anything you need, mate."

events.title: The recovery guy
events.speaker: mate
setup: {mate.short} has a 'recovery guy'. Little white pills in a plain tub. "Nothing on the list. They don't test for it. Your legs will thank you."
Your legs feel like concrete.

outcomes.text: You fly for a fortnight. Nobody asks. You keep the tub in your wash bag.
A random test, the Monday after. The sample does not come back clean.
He shrugs. "Your legs." You notice he does not offer twice.

choices.label: Tell the physio what he is handing round.

outcomes.text: The tub goes off to a lab. He is fined and dropped. He knows exactly who.
You leave the tub where it is and pull your boots on. {mate.short} shrugs and pockets it.

callbacks.line: "Didn't have you down as a grass."
"Your bloods came back odd. Anything you want to tell me?"

events.title: A letter from the ward
setup: The club forwards a letter. A boy on the children's ward, your shirt on the wall behind his bed. His operation is on Friday.
"Please could you say good luck. You are my best player."

outcomes.text: Two hours on the ward. {mate.short} does magic tricks, badly. The boy's mum films everything.

choices.label: Send a signed shirt and a note.

outcomes.text: His mum posts a photo of him holding it. It does well.
Somebody posts the letter with 'no reply'. It does better than the shirt would have.

callbacks.line: "Think about that kid a lot, you know. Hope he's all right."
Somebody has dug out the old letter again.

lines: "That's more like it. Did you see the gaffer's face at the end?"
"Don't read the papers this week. Trust me."
"The missus says you have to come round for tea. She's not asking."
He answers in one word. Then the headphones go back in.
"How did you deal with it? Your first season, I mean?"
"Look after your knees. Nobody tells you that."
"Still learning where everything is. Where do you sit in the canteen?"
"Saw the motor. What does that do, nought to sixty?"
"How's the horse? Is it actually fast or just good-looking?"
"Skipper. What's the gaffer really like with you?"
"My little brother has your poster up. Don't let it go to your head."
"One of us is starting Saturday. No hard feelings, whatever happens."
